# Data Model: Task-Oriented Command Surface Consolidation

Source TRD: [TRD-2026-87e64cc6-command-surface-consolidation.md](./TRD-2026-87e64cc6-command-surface-consolidation.md)
Source PRD: [PRD-2026-87e64cc6-command-surface-consolidation.md](../PRD/PRD-2026-87e64cc6-command-surface-consolidation.md)
Relevant REQ/AC refs: REQ-007 (AC-007-1, AC-007-2, AC-007-3), REQ-019 (AC-019-1, AC-019-2, AC-019-3, AC-019-4)

## Overview

This TRD introduces one new persisted schema — the **issue run record** — so `ensemble-issue fix` gets the same checkpointed, resumable run state the feature workflow (`ensemble-new-feature`) already has. Per the chosen architecture (Option C, see companion research doc), the existing feature `RunIndexStore` is *not* replaced or genericized at its public-API boundary; instead, its stage-agnostic I/O primitives (atomic write, active-lock acquire/release, optimistic-concurrency mutate, corruption validation) are extracted into a shared core module, and the issue workflow gets its own typed wrapper and `Stage` enum on top of that shared core — a sibling store, not a shared one. File/append-log-backed (JSON per run, same convention as the existing `.ensemble/new-feature/*.json` files); no relational database, no migration tooling.

## Entities

### IssueRunRecord (new)

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `runId` | string | random 8-hex id, same generation scheme as the feature `RunRecord.runId` |
| `projectRoot` | string | absolute path, matches the feature store's convention |
| `issueDescription` | string | the issue report or description this run started from; persisted so a later-session dispatch has input even without prior chat history (mirrors `RunRecord.idea`) |
| `status` | enum | `active` \| `paused` \| `completed` \| `abandoned` |
| `stage` | `IssueStage` (new) | `analysis_planning` \| `execution` \| `validation_delivery` \| `done` — one entry per fix-issue.yaml's own named workflow phases (`Analysis & Planning`, `Execution`, `Validation & Delivery`), plus the terminal `done` |
| `stageOutcome` | `StageOutcome` (reused, unchanged) | the existing `{ kind: "success" \| "decline" \| "failure" \| "approval_wait", detail?, recordedAt }` type from `new-feature/types.ts`, imported as-is — no issue-specific fork |
| `artifacts` | `IssueArtifactRef[]` (new) | see below; looser than the feature workflow's closed `"prd" \| "trd"` union because fix-issue's own output shape isn't fixed by this TRD |
| `beadRefs` | string[] | bead IDs, and `pr:<url>`-prefixed PR references — same convention as `RunRecord.beadRefs` (REQ-019 reuses this prefix rule rather than inventing a second one) |
| `prApprovedAt` | string \| null | ISO-8601; same semantics as `RunRecord.prApprovedAt` (REQ-014-2's boundary: only a real approval-checkpoint mutate sets this) |
| `revision` | integer | optimistic-concurrency counter, same contract as the feature store's `mutate(expectedRevision, …)` |
| `createdAt` / `updatedAt` | ISO-8601 timestamp | — |

### IssueArtifactRef (new)

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | string (free-form label, e.g. `"investigation-notes"`, `"fix-plan"`) | Not a closed enum like the PRD/TRD `ArtifactRef.type` — fix-issue's own output shape is out of this TRD's scope to redefine |
| `path` | string | repo-relative path to the artifact, when one is produced |
| `recordedAt` | ISO-8601 timestamp | — |

### RunIndexCorePrimitives (shared, not a persisted entity)

Not a schema of its own — the extracted stage-agnostic functions (`writeRunAtomic`, lock acquire/release, `mutate` with revision-conflict detection, corrupt-file validation) operate generically over whatever `TStage`/`TRecord` shape each workflow's thin wrapper supplies. Listed here only to make clear no new persisted fields live at this layer.

## Relationships

```text
IssueRunRecord   1 --- * IssueArtifactRef   (embedded array, not a separate file)
IssueRunRecord   * --- 1 projectRoot         (single active run per project, same REQ-008-equivalent exclusivity as the feature store's active.lock — AC-019-1)
IssueRunRecord   0..1 --- 1 "pr:<url>" beadRefs entry   (optional, same prefix convention as the feature store)
```

`IssueRunRecord` is structurally parallel to, but never joined with, the feature workflow's `RunRecord` — REQ-002 requires the two run stores stay independent; an issue run never references or is referenced by a feature run.

## Data Ownership

- **Ensemble owns:** `IssueRunRecord` files under `.ensemble/fix-issue/` (directory name chosen to parallel the existing `.ensemble/new-feature/` convention), local to the project working copy. Not a durable, cross-session production store — this is local checkpoint/resume state, same category as the existing feature run index (Constitution §1, Rule 4).
- **No external system owns or reads this schema** in this release; `beadRefs`/`pr:<url>` entries are references into systems (Beads, GitHub) that remain the system of record for their own data.

## Migration/Backfill Notes

Not applicable — greenfield schema, no existing issue run-state data to migrate. The extraction of shared primitives into the new core module (Option C) must not change the on-disk shape or file location of any existing `.ensemble/new-feature/*.json` file; the feature workflow's existing run files must continue to load unmodified after the refactor (regression check, see TRD-014-TEST).

## Validation Rules

- `IssueRunRecord.stage` must be one of the four `IssueStage` values; an unrecognized value is a corrupt-file error (`RUN_INDEX_CORRUPT`), never silently coerced — same contract as the feature store's `validateRunRecordShape`.
- Only one `active`/`paused` `IssueRunRecord` may exist per `projectRoot` at a time, enforced by the same active-lock mechanism the shared core provides (AC-019-1).
- `beadRefs` entries carrying the `pr:` prefix are the only way to represent a PR reference; a bare bead ID is never itself a PR reference (same rule as the feature store, reused verbatim for consistency per REQ-003's product-wide-invariant decision).

## Privacy/Security Notes

- `IssueRunRecord`/`IssueArtifactRef` are local-only checkpoint data; `issueDescription` may echo the content of a user-reported issue, which could itself contain sensitive details the reporter included — no new field here increases exposure beyond what the issue report already contained, and no credential material is ever stored in this schema (Constitution Non-Negotiable Rule 1).

## Open Questions

None — all fields above are fully specified by this TRD; any remaining implementation-detail choices (exact JSON key ordering, temp-file naming scheme) are covered by reusing the shared core's existing, already-tested behavior rather than introducing new unspecified behavior.
